# `⌸` — Key

Monadic operator. Keys: `Alt-q =`

`K f⌸Y` groups major cells of `Y` by corresponding keys in `K`. Calls `key f group`; groups appear in first-occurrence order.

```bpl
1 1 2{+/⍵}⌸10 20 30 ⍝ 30 30
```

`f⌸Y` uses `Y` as keys and their positions as values.

Keys match with [tolerance](../evaluation.qmd#equality-and-ordering), as in `≠`. Results assemble with fill. Empty input calls `f` once for its prototype.

## Fast combinations

These trains and compositions give the result of applying their parts in turn, faster. [Trains](../evaluation.qmd#trains) says which spellings BPL recognises.

| Combination | Applies to | Benefit |
|---|---|---|
| `≢⊢ ⌸Y` or `K (≢⊢)⌸Y` | any keys | counts each group's major cells without building the groups |
| `K (f/⊢)⌸Y` or `K (f⌿⊢)⌸Y`, with `f` of `+ ⌈ ⌊`, or `×` of floats | a vector `Y` of floats, integers or Booleans | folds every group in one pass, without a call of the operand for each group |

```bpl
≢⊢ ⌸"banana"          ⍝ [1 3 2]ₓ
1 1 2(+/⊢)⌸10 20 30   ⍝ 30 30
```
